sections.h2: Which Escambia office sends the bill?
sections.html:
Billing and collection belong to the Escambia County Tax Collector, and valuation and the roll belong to the Property Appraiser. The appraiser's roll covers Escambia County, the City of Pensacola and the Town of Century, and its site notes that assessment values and exemptions reflect the 2026 certified tax roll.

The Tax Collector's office collects for the District School Board, the Board of County Commissioners, the City of Pensacola, the Town of Century, the Sheriff, the Downtown Improvement Board and the Northwest Florida Water Management District. It also collects for several state agencies. You can search a bill by name, address or account number on the Tax Collector's site, sign up for paperless e-billing, and read posted reports, including a list of the top 25 taxpayers in the county.

sections.h2: What is the payment schedule for Escambia County bills?
sections.html:
Bills are normally mailed November 1 and can be paid early at a discount that shrinks each month. Escambia's Tax Collector prints the schedule as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February and the gross amount in March.

Escambia County tax collection schedule printed by the Tax Collector
PeriodWhat applies
November 1Notices mailed addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1
November4 percent discount
December3 percent discount
January2 percent discount
February1 percent discount
MarchGross amount
April 1Delinquent: 3 percent penalty on real estate, 1.5 percent on tangible property
May 1Advertising costs begin to be added

A missed bill does not excuse late payment. The office reminds owners it is their duty to find out the amount due and pay before April 1, and the same rule applies if a bill went to an old address. Send address changes to the Property Appraiser, who maintains the roll.

sections.h2: What non-ad valorem charges show up on an Escambia County bill?
sections.html:
Some line items are flat assessments that do not depend on your home's value, and the charge depends on whether the house is inside Pensacola or in the unincorporated county. Unpaid non-ad valorem amounts can lead to a tax certificate just like unpaid property tax.

  • Unincorporated Escambia: the Board of County Commissioners assesses fire protection, rescue and advanced life support, street lighting, road paving, retention ponds and solid waste. For amounts, call the County Office of Management and Budget at (850) 595-4960.
  • Inside Pensacola: the City Council assesses stormwater management, based on the square footage of impervious surface on the property. For amounts, call the City of Pensacola at (850) 436-5646.

When you sell, look at the bill's non-ad valorem section as well as the main levy, because a buyer or title agent will ask whether these were paid.

sections.h2: What does Florida's homestead rule mean for Escambia County owners?
sections.html:
An owner who makes a Florida home the permanent residence by January 1 can apply for up to $50,000 in homestead exemption. The application goes to the county property appraiser, using Form DR-501, by March 1 of the tax year.

Once granted, Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to the smaller of 3 percent or the CPI change. DOR's chart prints a cap of 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. Assessed value on non-homestead property is limited to a 10 percent annual increase.

The shield ends when the property is sold. Florida DOR says a change of ownership resets value to just value on the following January 1. That matters for your buyer's first bill, so it helps to tell buyers that Escambia's tax on the house will likely rise after they close.

sections.h2: How do I dispute an Escambia County assessment?
sections.html:
Challenge the value after the August notice arrives, and do it quickly. Florida DOR says a petition on one of the DR-486 forms goes to the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and the same notice lists the dates when the School Board, the county and the City of Pensacola hold budget hearings.

Exemption problems run on another track. If the Property Appraiser denies an exemption, classification, portability transfer or tax deferral, the Value Adjustment Board petition is due 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. Growth in a taxing body's property tax revenue is also capped by state law at per capita personal income growth plus new construction unless a super-majority, unanimous vote or referendum overrides the cap, which is why hearings in September and October can change your rate even when your value stays flat.

Keep every notice you receive. A buyer's agent may ask for the TRIM notice to see what your neighbors' proposed rates look like in the same district.

sections.h2: What happens if Escambia County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After April 1, the county sells a tax certificate on the unpaid amount, and the property can eventually be lost through a tax deed. The Escambia Tax Collector says failure to pay results in a certificate and may result in loss of the property at a future date.

  • Florida statute awards each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps, and unsold certificates go to the county at the maximum rate.
  • The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the year of issuance, and the application fee is $75.
  • On a tax deed sale, the opening bid on a homestead includes half of the latest assessed value in addition to the amounts due.
  • Notice goes to the titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders and recorded contract-for-deed vendees.

A seller with certificates outstanding can still close, with the redemption cost coming off the proceeds. Request a payoff statement from the Tax Collector well ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Can a senior, veteran or disabled owner in Escambia County pay less?
sections.html:
Florida has several reductions. None apply on their own, so the owner files for each.

  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a homestead discount equal to their VA disability percentage.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more receives a $5,000 reduction.
  • Homestead deferral: file Form DR-570 with the Tax Collector by March 31 after the assessment year. The deferred share is the tax above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.
  • An ordinance may add up to $50,000 for owners past 65 who meet an income test.

Ask the Escambia County Property Appraiser which of these the county has adopted and what the current limits are before you rely on one.

sections.h2: What closing steps involve Escambia taxes and title?
sections.html:
Clear the tax account first, then plan for deed stamps. Deed documentary stamp tax in Escambia County is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, due through the clerk at recording, and each party to the deed is liable for it.

If the house is escrowed, the mortgage company pays within the discount period, so ask your servicer what has been paid and when a refund follows payoff. For a property that has passed through probate or has unrecorded heirs, you may need the clerk's records on the estate before the buyer's title agent will insure.

faqs.q: When does Escambia County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: Normally November 1 each year, addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. If you do not get one, ask the Tax Collector, because the duty to pay before April 1 stays with the owner.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Escambia County property tax?
faqs.a: A 3 percent penalty is added to real estate bills on April 1, and 1.5 percent to tangible property bills. Advertising costs start being added May 1, and a certificate can follow.

faqs.q: Whom do I phone about a stormwater or fire line on my Escambia bill?
faqs.a: For unincorporated Escambia, call the County Office of Management and Budget at (850) 595-4960. For the Pensacola stormwater charge, call the City of Pensacola at (850) 436-5646.

faqs.q: Does my Escambia County homestead cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property resets to just value the following January 1. Portability can carry part of your cap to your next Florida home.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Escambia County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, and any certificate redemption, comes out of the proceeds. Request a payoff statement from the Tax Collector well ahead of closing.
